label: Week to Sunday 22 November 2026
compiled: Compiled 22 Nov 2026 from published incident reports; this is not a live attack feed.

legend.red: Confirmed major breach or disruptive attack reported this week
legend.yellow: Smaller incident, attempted attack or unconfirmed claim
legend.green: Good news: arrests, fixes or takedowns

top.t: FBI investigates a breach of its criminal information database
top.d: The apparent breach follows tech outages that hit banking and air traffic control the week before.

top.t: Nearly nine million Peach Aviation customer records leaked
top.d: The Japanese airline confirmed the leak on 20 November after an attack on its outside email service provider.

top.t: Europe's month of cyberattacks: 16 incidents mapped
top.d: Industry group DigitalEurope counted 16 incidents between 18 October and 18 November, 11 of them cyberattacks, including supermarket freezers switched to defrost.

top.t: Ransomware gang lists Nvidia; Nvidia sees no breach
top.d: The Gentlemen group put Nvidia on its leak site. Nvidia says its investigation found no sign its systems were compromised.
235 servers and 257 domains linked to the Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware were taken offline.

840.d: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database.

392.d: Peach Aviation confirmed that 8,997,106 customer records leaked after an attack on its email service provider.

112.d: A ransomware attack on a Belarusian cloud firm disrupted businesses for days.

124.d: Bell Canada reported the theft of enterprise telecom-circuit customer data; it said no credentials were taken and services were unaffected.

231.d: Ethiopian Airlines' ShebaMiles loyalty programme reported a data breach.

578.d: A suspected attempted cyberattack on an energy company was reported on 17 November.

276.d: This month shops lost frozen food to the freezer hacks, a military drone maker was hit through a hijacked software update, and personal data of senior German officials was published.

250.d: Several blood banks were hit in this month's refrigeration attacks. French agencies blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards for a similar hack in October.

380.d: Shops threw away spoiled food after the freezer hacks, and personal data of senior Italian officials was published.

528.d: Shops threw away spoiled food after this month's freezer hacks, and personal data of senior Dutch officials was published.

056.d: Shops threw away spoiled meat and frozen food after this month's freezer hacks.

752.d: Shops threw away spoiled meat and frozen food after this month's freezer hacks.

642.d: Espionage malware was found in government email, and shops were hit by this month's freezer hacks.

356.d: The LockBit5 ransomware group claimed to have targeted travel firm Yatra; the claim is unconfirmed.

826.d: A British cybersecurity operation fixed the flaw in commercial fridges and freezers that was used in the European hacks.

804.d: Ukrainian police and the FBI arrested four suspected members of a ransomware gang linked to more than $40.5 million in ransoms.
